proposed_comments.body:
### Give users control over the editor-wide I shortcut

**Severity:** `low` (non-blocking accessibility design improvement)

**Affected code:** `src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Views/ColorEditorView.xaml:11-14` and `ColorEditorView.xaml.cs:36-37,78-91`.

**Problem:** The root Grid declares an unconditional, unmodified `I` accelerator. `ShouldStartPicking` excludes text input and the Adjust color flyout, but there is no control-specific focus restriction or setting to disable or remap this editor shortcut. Changing the configurable activation hotkey does not change this separate XAML declaration.

**Why it matters:** Users who need to avoid single-character commands have no way to keep the editor available while opting out of this one. The character-key-shortcut guidance in [WCAG 2.1.4](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts.html) describes three alternatives: turn it off, remap it to include a non-character modifier, or activate it only when the relevant control has focus. This is a source-level design observation, not a claim that a particular speech-input or key-repeat failure has been reproduced.

**Suggested change:**

1. Choose one supported path: add an editor-shortcut enable/remap setting, or restrict `I` to the Pick button's focus scope. If editor-wide unmodified `I` is intentional, prefer an opt-out to preserve that workflow for users who want it.
2. Wire that choice into the accelerator registration or `PickAccelerator_Invoked` eligibility check; changing the global activation hotkey alone must not be used as the opt-out.
3. Preserve the existing text-input/flyout guards and the normal button command. Cover the selected scope or configuration in the shortcut tests.

**Verification:** For an opt-out/remap implementation, verify persistence and confirm that the original `I` no longer invokes picking when disabled/remapped. For a focus-scoped implementation, verify that `I` invokes picking only with the Pick button focused. In either case, check history-list and other-control focus, typed hex input, an open Adjust color flyout, and normal button activation.
